assessments.title: Anxiety Check
assessments.subtitle: A quick, validated screen for anxiety symptoms.
assessments.description: A couple of minutes to check in on how anxious or on edge you've been feeling lately. Seven short questions about the past two weeks — answer honestly and you'll get a clear, private sense of where things stand, with a gentle next step if you want one. It's based on the GAD-7, a screening questionnaire used widely by health professionals.
assessments.disclaimer: This is a self-check, not a diagnosis. Only a qualified professional can diagnose an anxiety disorder.
assessments.instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?

questions.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it's hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

results.headline: Your anxiety levels look low right now
results.body: Your responses suggest minimal anxiety over the past two weeks. A good moment to build habits that keep it that way.

results.headline: Some signs of mild anxiety
results.body: You're showing some symptoms of anxiety. This is common and very manageable with the right tools. The Anxiety journey is a good place to start.

results.headline: Moderate anxiety symptoms
results.body: Your responses point to a moderate level of anxiety. Self-help tools can help, and it may be worth talking to someone. Consider booking a counsellor.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

results.headline: Significant anxiety symptoms
results.body: Your responses suggest a high level of anxiety. You don't have to manage this on your own — speaking to a professional is a strong next step.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

assessments.title: Mood Check
assessments.subtitle: A validated screen for low mood and depression.
assessments.description: A short, private check-in on how your mood has been over the past two weeks. Nine questions, with no right or wrong answers — just answer as honestly as you can, and you'll see a clear picture of how you've been doing, along with support that fits. It's based on the PHQ-9, used widely by health professionals.
assessments.disclaimer: This is a self-check, not a diagnosis. Only a qualified professional can diagnose depression.
assessments.instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following?

questions.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure, or that you have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed — or the opposite, being so fidgety or restless that you've been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

safety.note: If q9 is answered with any value above 0, show this safety screen FIRST, before the band result, regardless of total score.
safety.headline: Let's pause for a moment
safety.body: One of your answers suggests you've had thoughts that you'd be better off dead, or of hurting yourself. That can be a heavy and frightening thing to carry — and you don't have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone today. Talking to a real person can make a genuine difference.

cta.label: Talk to someone now on AskNelson

results.headline: Your mood looks steady right now
results.body: Your responses suggest minimal symptoms of low mood over the past two weeks. Keep doing what supports you.

results.headline: Some signs of low mood
results.body: You're showing some mild symptoms. Movement, sleep, and connection all help — and small, consistent steps matter most.

results.headline: Moderate symptoms of depression
results.body: Your responses point to a moderate level of low mood. This is worth taking seriously — talking to a professional is a good next step.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

results.headline: Moderately severe symptoms
results.body: Your responses suggest a significant level of depression symptoms. Please consider speaking to a professional soon — support helps, and you deserve it.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

results.headline: Severe symptoms of depression
results.body: Your responses suggest a high level of depression symptoms. You don't have to manage this alone — reaching out to a professional is an important step to take now.

assessments.title: Burnout Check
assessments.subtitle: Measure exhaustion, cynicism, and sense of effectiveness.
assessments.description: Feeling worn down? These twelve questions look at the past month across the three sides of burnout — how drained you feel, how connected you are to your work, and how effective you feel doing it. You'll see not just whether you're running low, but what's driving it, so you know where to start.
assessments.disclaimer: This is a self-check to help you reflect, not a clinical diagnosis.
assessments.instructions: Thinking about the past month, how often have you felt each of the following?

questions.text: I feel emotionally drained by my work or daily responsibilities
I feel used up at the end of the day
I feel tired when I wake up and have to face another day
I have little energy left for the people and things outside of work
I feel less interested in my work than I used to
I've become more cynical about whether what I do matters
I feel detached or distant from the people I work with
I just want to get through the day rather than do things well
I feel confident that I'm effective at what I do
I feel I'm making a meaningful contribution
I can deal well with the problems that come up
I feel a sense of accomplishment from what I do

scoring.reverse_note: For questions marked reverse:true, score as (scale_max - response), so that higher always means more burnout.

results.headline: You're in a sustainable place
results.body: Your responses suggest a low risk of burnout right now. Worth protecting — notice what's working and keep it.

results.headline: Early warning signs
results.body: You're showing some early signs of burnout. This is the best time to act, before it builds. Check the dimension breakdown to see where the pressure is coming from.

results.headline: Moderate burnout
results.body: Your responses point to a meaningful level of burnout. The Burnout journey is built exactly for this — and it may be worth talking to someone too.

results.headline: High burnout
results.body: Your responses suggest you're significantly burned out. Recovery is possible, but it takes more than a weekend off. Consider both the Burnout journey and speaking to a professional.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

dimension_flags.note: If any single dimension is at or above its high_threshold, show a short flag even when the overall band is lower.
dimension_flags.exhaustion: Your exhaustion levels are high — rest and recovery are the priority here.
dimension_flags.cynicism: You're feeling detached from your work — a sign to reconnect with what gives it meaning.
dimension_flags.efficacy: Your sense of effectiveness has dropped — this often recovers as exhaustion eases.

assessments.title: Sleep Quality Check
assessments.subtitle: See how well you're really sleeping.
assessments.description: A quick, honest look at how you've really been sleeping over the past two weeks — how long you take to drop off, how often you wake, and how it's shaping your days. Eight questions to help you see what's working and what might need a little attention.
assessments.disclaimer: This is a self-check, not a diagnosis. Persistent sleep problems are worth discussing with a doctor.
assessments.instructions: Thinking about the past two weeks, answer as honestly as you can.

questions.text: How long does it usually take you to fall asleep?
On an average night, how many hours of sleep do you actually get?
How often do you wake during the night and struggle to fall back asleep?
How often do you wake earlier than you want to and can't get back to sleep?
How would you rate your overall sleep quality lately?
How often does poor sleep affect your mood, focus, or energy during the day?
How consistent are your sleep and wake times from day to day?
How often do racing thoughts or worry keep you awake?

results.headline: Your sleep looks healthy
results.body: Your responses suggest you're sleeping well. Protect the habits that are working for you.

results.headline: Some sleep disruption
results.body: Your sleep is being disrupted in a few ways. Small changes to routine and wind-down often make a real difference here.

results.headline: Moderate sleep problems
results.body: Your sleep is meaningfully disrupted. The Sleep theme has practical, evidence-based steps to help you reset.

results.headline: Significant sleep problems
results.body: Your sleep is significantly disrupted. Self-help can help, but ongoing problems like this are worth raising with a doctor.

assessments.title: Relationship Health Check
assessments.subtitle: A reflection on your closest relationship.
assessments.description: A moment to step back and reflect on your closest relationship. Ten honest questions about communication, trust, closeness, and how supported you feel. It's written with a romantic partner in mind, but works for any close relationship — and it's a reflection, not a verdict.
assessments.disclaimer: This is a reflection tool, not a verdict on your relationship. It can't capture everything — trust your own judgement.
assessments.instructions: Thinking about your relationship over the past while, how much do you agree with each statement?

questions.text: I can be open and honest with my partner
My partner really listens when I talk about what matters to me
I trust my partner
When we disagree, we're able to work through it respectfully
Our arguments often leave me feeling hurt or disrespected
I feel emotionally close to my partner
I feel supported by my partner during stressful times
I often feel lonely even when we're together
I feel valued and respected in this relationship
Overall, I'm satisfied with this relationship

scoring.reverse_note: For questions marked reverse:true, score as (scale_max - response). Higher total means a healthier relationship.

results.headline: A strong, healthy relationship
results.body: Your responses suggest a relationship that's working well across the things that matter most. Keep investing in it.

results.headline: Healthy, with room to grow
results.body: Your relationship is generally in good shape, with a few areas worth attention. Small, consistent effort goes a long way.

results.headline: Some real strain
results.body: Your responses point to meaningful strain in the relationship. The Relationships theme has tools for communication and connection — and talking it through, together or with a counsellor, can help.

results.headline: The relationship is under real pressure
results.body: Your responses suggest the relationship is struggling across several areas. That's hard to sit in. Support — through honest conversation or a counsellor — can make a difference.

cta.label: Talk to a counsellor on AskNelson

results.safety_note: If you ever feel unsafe, controlled, or afraid in your relationship, that is different from relationship difficulty — and confidential support is available.
